name: UCSF Summer Student Research Program (SSRP)
title: Structured Summer Research Program

summary: Seven-week, one-on-one mentored biomedical research placement with UCSF researchers, ending in a research symposium where students present findings. For the 2026 cohort, eligibility is limited to high schoolers considered under-represented in the sciences (first-generation, low-income, disabled, or otherwise disadvantaged backgrounds).

name: Duke Cell Biology Academy (CeBA)
title: Structured Summer Research Program
applicationWindow: 2026 deadline was March 20; program ran June 22 – July 31, 2026. Applications for 2027 typically open in January.
ratingNote: Paid ($2,400) independent research project with a real Duke mentor, ending in a poster session — but limited to students who can commute daily to campus (Research Triangle area).
summary: Six-week paid research internship pairing high school juniors/seniors with a Duke Cell Biology graduate student or postdoc mentor on an independent project, ending in a poster session. Students must arrange their own transportation to Duke's campus every day — no housing or transportation is provided.

name: Scripps Research REACH Summer Internship
title: Structured Summer Research Program
applicationWindow: 2026 application closed March 22. Only open to students at specific REACH partner high schools in the San Diego area — confirm the current partner school list before planning around this one.
ratingNote: Strong, prestigious lab experience at a major research institute — but eligibility is restricted to students currently enrolled at a short list of partner high schools in San Diego County, so most students nationally can't apply at all.
summary: Seven-week paid lab internship with a Scripps Research mentor, preceded by a short training bootcamp. Eligibility is restricted to students currently enrolled at specific REACH partner high schools in the San Diego area — check the current partner list on the program site before counting on this one.

name: Rutgers Waksman Student Scholars Program (WSSP)
title: Teacher-Mediated Year-Long Research Program
applicationWindow: Works differently from the others: a student's own science teacher applies to attend a summer Institute (deadline is typically around March 1), then runs the year-long project with students at school.
ratingNote: Genuine, publication-quality molecular biology/bioinformatics research — but a student can only take part if a teacher at their own school signs up first, so it's not something you can apply for individually.
summary: A year-long program where a science teacher attends a Rutgers summer Institute, then leads a real molecular biology and bioinformatics research project with students at their own high school during the academic year. You'll need a science teacher at your school willing to get involved — this isn't an individual application.

name: High School Research Academy (HSRA)
title: Structured Summer Research Program
applicationWindow: 2026 cycle closed (deadline was March 22). Opens again in January 2027.
ratingNote: Real hands-on lab research and college credit at a major research university — but this is a paid program with a $4,000 fee (non-refundable $400 deposit on acceptance), not a stipend, so weigh cost against prestige. Texas residents are currently prioritized.
summary: Five-week, in-person research placement in an active UT Austin lab, earning 3 hours of college credit through an extension course. No housing or transportation provided. Costs $4,000 total, due after a position is offered — some students may want to ask about need-based flexibility before ruling it out.

name: Secondary School Field Research Program (SSFRP)
title: Structured Summer Research Program
applicationWindow: Applications are typically due by March 31 each year (2026 cycle closed).
ratingNote: Genuine six-week field and lab research on real environmental questions, with a stipend for participants — strong resume value, but it runs through a small number of partner NYC-area schools with a teacher liaison rather than a simple individual online application.
summary: Six weeks of hands-on wetland ecology and environmental field research at the Piermont Marsh site, working in teams with Columbia scientists and undergraduate mentors. Students receive a stipend. Participation is organized through a science teacher at each participating school, who helps select students — check with a science teacher first about whether your school is involved.

name: Hofstra Summer Science Research Program (HUSSRP)
title: Structured Summer Research Program
department: Multiple (Biology, Chemistry, Psychology, Public Health, Engineering)
applicationWindow: 2026 cycle closed (deadline was February 2, 2026). Typically opens in fall/winter for the following summer.
ratingNote: Solid faculty-mentored research ending in a poster session, and admission is genuinely competitive — but this is a paid (tuition-style) program, roughly $2,250+ depending on the year, plus a non-refundable application fee, rather than a paid stipend position.
summary: Four-week, on-campus research placement matched to a Hofstra faculty mentor, ending in a poster session. Requires a teacher recommendation and an interview. Costs roughly $2,250+ (varies by year) plus a non-refundable application fee — some scholarship support may be available, so it's worth asking.

name: Kimberly Querrey Summer Research Program
title: Structured Summer Research Program
university: Northwestern University — Feinberg School of Medicine
applicationWindow: Currently NOT accepting new applications — the program is working through a backlog of previously submitted applications after a cancelled cycle. Confirm current status on the program site before planning around this one.
ratingNote: Paid, genuinely hands-on biomedical research at a major medical school, contributing to real lung-disease research — strong pick when it's open, but it is not currently accepting new applicants, so its usefulness right now depends entirely on when it reopens.
summary: Six-to-eight week paid research experience for rising high school seniors and undergrads, working on real lung-disease research projects with Northwestern faculty, ending in a symposium presentation. The program is currently prioritizing previously submitted applications and is not accepting new submissions for the upcoming cycle — check back on their site for updates.

name: Stanford Chemistry Undergraduate Research
title: Direct Faculty Contact & Summer Research Fellowship
applicationWindow: Academic-year lab positions: no deadline, contact faculty anytime. Paid Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship: application opens each February, deadline in early April (2025 deadline was April 7).
ratingNote: The paid summer fellowship (around $8,000+ stipend) is excellent on paper — but both routes described here are open only to students who are ALREADY enrolled Stanford undergraduates. This is not an outreach program and isn't actually accessible to outside high schoolers or undergrads at other universities, which is why it's rated low despite the prestige.
summary: IMPORTANT: this is only open to current Stanford undergraduates. During the academic year, Stanford undergrads can contact Chemistry faculty directly about joining their lab (similar to a Direct Outreach listing). Separately, the department runs a paid 10-week Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship each summer. Neither route is open to students outside Stanford's own undergraduate population — included here mainly so current Stanford students browsing this site can find it.

name: Development & Education Lab (DEL Lab)
title: Open Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: No fixed application cycle. Availability varies by semester; students should email the lab directly.
ratingNote: A solid opportunity for students interested in psychology research. While not a formal internship, it provides meaningful exposure to university research through volunteer work and shadowing.
summary: The DEL Lab offers high school shadowing and volunteer opportunities when space is available. Interested students submit a letter of interest and résumé directly to the lab. Availability changes each semester, making this an inquiry-based opportunity rather than a structured program.

name: Yale Chemistry Faculty Labs
title: Faculty Sponsorship Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling throughout the year. Requires faculty sponsorship before participation.
ratingNote: An outstanding opportunity for motivated high school students, but highly dependent on successfully finding a Yale faculty member willing to sponsor the student.
summary: Qualified high school students (typically ages 16–17) may participate in Yale chemistry research if a faculty member agrees to sponsor them. There is no centralized application process, so students must first secure a research mentor.

name: Rutgers NJ Medical School Faculty Labs
title: Direct Faculty Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling. Students arrange placements directly with individual faculty members.
ratingNote: Excellent opportunity for students interested in biomedical research. Success depends on contacting faculty members individually and finding a mentor willing to supervise.
summary: Rutgers NJ Medical School allows motivated high school students to independently arrange laboratory research experiences with faculty members. Students must satisfy university requirements for minors working in research laboratories.

name: Loyola Biology Research Labs
title: Faculty Research Opportunities
applicationWindow: Faculty may be contacted throughout the academic year.
ratingNote: A good undergraduate research opportunity where students directly contact faculty members. Not intended for high school students but useful for future college users.
summary: Loyola encourages undergraduate students to browse faculty research profiles and contact professors conducting projects that interest them. The department also provides guidance on writing effective research inquiry emails.

name: Cleveland Clinic Research Laboratories
title: Direct Faculty Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling. Seasonal internship opportunities may also become available.
ratingNote: A highly respected biomedical research institution offering exceptional laboratory experience. Students should expect to contact multiple investigators before securing a placement.
summary: The Cleveland Clinic Lerner Research Institute encourages students to identify research laboratories of interest and contact principal investigators directly with a résumé, transcript, and statement of interest. Students may need to reach out to several faculty members before finding an available mentor.

name: Computer Science & Informatics Research Experience (CSIRE)
title: Structured Summer Research Program
applicationWindow: Applications typically open in January and close in March.
ratingNote: One of the strongest computer science research opportunities available to high school students. Participants conduct genuine faculty-led research while receiving mentorship from graduate students and researchers.
summary: The CSIRE program places high school students into active computer science and biomedical informatics research laboratories at Stony Brook University. Students conduct projects involving artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, visualization, machine learning, and human-computer interaction while working alongside faculty, PhD students, and postdoctoral researchers.

name: Research Program for High School Students
title: Structured Summer Research Program
university: The University of Texas at Dallas
applicationWindow: Applications generally open in January with a priority deadline around March 1.
ratingNote: A highly competitive research opportunity that provides meaningful faculty mentorship and authentic computer science research experience for high school students.
summary: This eight-week summer research program allows advanced high school students to participate in real-world computer science research projects under university faculty. Students may earn recommendation letters based on their research performance.

name: Mentor Assistance Program (MAP)
title: Faculty Mentorship Research Program
applicationWindow: Applications typically open in late summer for the academic year.
ratingNote: An exceptional interdisciplinary mentorship program connecting high school students with UC San Diego faculty conducting cutting-edge STEM research.
summary: The Mentor Assistance Program matches high school students with faculty mentors across disciplines including computer science, physics, biochemistry, neuroscience, and nanoengineering. Students work on authentic research projects throughout the academic year.

name: Research Experience for High School Students (REHS)
title: Supercomputing Research Program
applicationWindow: Applications generally open in February and close around March 15.
ratingNote: An outstanding opportunity for students interested in computational science and high-performance computing. Students work directly with researchers at one of the nation's leading supercomputing centers.
summary: Students spend eight weeks conducting computational science research involving artificial intelligence, scientific visualization, supercomputing, and high-performance computing alongside researchers at the San Diego Supercomputer Center.

name: Imperial College Physics School Research Outreach
title: Physics Research & School Engagement Opportunity
applicationWindow: No fixed application window. Schools and colleges interested in engagement opportunities are encouraged to contact the Space and Atmospheric Physics group directly.
ratingNote: A potentially valuable opportunity for high school students interested in physics, particularly space and atmospheric physics. Unlike a structured internship, participation depends on available school engagement and research outreach opportunities, so students or schools should inquire directly.
summary: Imperial College London's Space and Atmospheric Physics group works with school students and teachers through physics outreach and longer-term engagement activities. Schools and colleges interested in working with the group can contact them about available opportunities. This listing replaces the former PRiSE listing because a current dedicated PRiSE application page could not be verified.

name: Hanbin Mao — Mao Research Lab
title: Direct Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling. The lab is currently recruiting high school students; interested students should contact Dr. Hanbin Mao directly.
ratingNote: An unusually strong direct-inquiry opportunity for high school students because the lab already hosts high school researchers and is actively seeking additional students. Participants may gain experience with highly specialized single-molecule, chemical, and molecular biology research.
summary: The Mao Research Lab studies mechanical forces and interactions involving biomolecules using single-molecule techniques. Research spans mechanoanalytical chemistry, DNA and protein behavior, molecular biology, and biophysics. The lab currently includes high school researchers and is seeking additional high school students, making this a rare direct-access university laboratory opportunity.

name: Ran Blekhman — Blekhman Lab
title: Direct Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling with no fixed application deadline listed. Interested high school students may contact Professor Blekhman with a short introduction and CV.
ratingNote: A rare opportunity for high school students to directly inquire about computational genomics research at a major research university. Particularly strong for students with programming or computational experience who want exposure to genomics, machine learning, and microbiome research.
summary: The Blekhman Lab studies interactions between human genetics, the microbiome, and health using computational genomics. Its research incorporates machine learning, population genetics, sequencing, and multi-omics approaches. The lab explicitly welcomes inquiries from high school students and asks interested students to contact Professor Blekhman with a brief introduction and CV.

name: Andrés Vidal-Gadea — Vidal-Gadea Lab
title: Direct Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling. Interested students should contact the lab directly about currently available research opportunities.
ratingNote: An exceptional niche research opportunity for motivated high school students. Previous high school researchers have participated in behavioral testing, microscopy, immunohistochemistry, and data analysis connected to ongoing laboratory research.
summary: The Vidal-Gadea Lab conducts highly specialized neurobiology and neurogenetics research involving C. elegans and other animal models. Projects include Duchenne muscular dystrophy, animal magnetoreception, crayfish neurogenetics, and the biological effects of simulated extraterrestrial environments. The lab explicitly welcomes driven high school students to inquire about ongoing research opportunities.

name: Robert Landick — Landick Lab
title: Direct Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling. High school students may contact the lab about summer or academic-year opportunities, while undergraduate research opportunities are also available.
ratingNote: A particularly strong molecular biology opportunity because the lab explicitly invites high school students to inquire and states that prior research experience is not required. Research can provide exposure to advanced molecular biology, transcription, and synthetic biology techniques.
summary: The Landick Lab studies the molecular mechanisms controlling gene expression, with particular emphasis on RNA polymerase and transcription. Research includes transcriptional regulation, single-molecule approaches, synthetic biology, and bioenergy. Interested high school students are specifically encouraged to contact the lab, and prior research experience is not required.

name: Hillel Chiel — Chiel Lab
title: Volunteer Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling with no fixed application deadline listed. Interested students should contact Dr. Hillel Chiel directly with their research interests and a one-page résumé.
ratingNote: A strong direct-access university research opportunity for both high school and undergraduate students. The lab explicitly encourages student volunteers and provides a pathway for students to become involved with ongoing research projects.
summary: The Chiel Lab studies the neural and biomechanical mechanisms underlying animal behavior and motor control using experimental and computational approaches. High school and undergraduate students are explicitly encouraged to volunteer. Interested students can contact Dr. Hillel Chiel with their research interests and a one-page résumé.

name: Ryoko Oono — Oono Lab
title: Direct Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling with no fixed deadline listed. Highly motivated students from outside UCSB, including high school students, may contact Dr. Ryoko Oono about available projects and volunteer opportunities. UCSB students receive priority.
ratingNote: An unusually accessible ecology and evolutionary biology opportunity because the lab explicitly welcomes inquiries from high school students and students outside UCSB. Opportunities are competitive and UCSB students receive priority, but small research projects may be available to motivated outside students.
summary: The Oono Lab studies fungal biology, ecology, evolution, and interactions between fungi, plants, and other organisms. Highly motivated students from outside UC Santa Barbara, including high school students, may inquire about research projects and volunteer opportunities. Small summer projects may sometimes be available, although space is limited and UCSB students generally receive priority.

name: Tatiana Segura — Segura Lab
title: Direct Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling based on mentor and project availability. High school students may inquire directly about mentorship, while non-Duke undergraduates who will be local during the summer may also contact the lab about possible projects.
ratingNote: An exceptional direct-inquiry opportunity at a major biomedical engineering research lab. The lab explicitly welcomes high school students, and previous students have participated in wet-lab experiments, coding, and data analysis under mentorship from graduate students and postdoctoral researchers.
summary: The Segura Lab at Duke University develops biomaterials and regenerative medicine approaches for tissue repair and biomedical applications. The lab explicitly welcomes high school students interested in research mentorship. Previous high school projects have included wet-lab experiments, coding, and data analysis. Non-Duke undergraduates who will be local during the summer may also inquire about available projects.

name: Diehl Lab
title: Direct Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling. High school students are encouraged to email the lab directly for information about available opportunities. Undergraduate applicants may submit a résumé or CV, unofficial transcript, and course schedule.
ratingNote: A strong behavioral neuroscience opportunity because the lab explicitly welcomes high school students rather than limiting research positions to enrolled university students. Undergraduate students also have a clearly defined pathway for applying to ongoing research projects.
summary: The Diehl Lab at Kansas State University conducts behavioral neuroscience and psychology research. High school students are explicitly welcomed and may email the lab directly to ask about research involvement. Undergraduate students can also apply to participate in ongoing projects by submitting a résumé or CV, unofficial transcript, and course schedule.

name: Andrew Leber — Cognitive Control Laboratory
title: Direct Inquiry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Rolling. The laboratory frequently recruits undergraduate research assistants and high school students. Undergraduate applications are accepted continuously, with interviews conducted when positions become available.
ratingNote: A strong psychology and neuroscience opportunity with unusually explicit access for high school students. The lab recruits students on a rolling basis and provides exposure to active research on attention, distraction, visual processing, and cognitive control.
summary: The Cognitive Control Laboratory at The Ohio State University studies how people control attention, respond to distraction, and adapt cognitive processes based on goals and experience. The lab frequently recruits both undergraduate research assistants and high school students. Interested students can contact the laboratory directly, while undergraduate applications are accepted continuously and interviews occur as positions become available.

name: Eugene Koay — Cancer Physics & Engineering Lab
title: Summer Research Internship Opportunity
applicationWindow: Summer research opportunities are offered based on lab availability. High school and college students interested in a summer experience or internship are instructed to contact Dr. Eugene Koay directly.
ratingNote: An exceptional direct-access opportunity for students interested in medicine, oncology, biomedical engineering, or cancer research. The lab explicitly advertises summer experiences for both high school and college students at one of the world's leading cancer research centers.
summary: The Cancer Physics & Engineering Lab at UT MD Anderson Cancer Center conducts interdisciplinary research involving cancer, physics, engineering, imaging, and oncology. The lab explicitly offers summer experiences and internships for high school and college students. Interested students are instructed to email Dr. Eugene Koay directly about potential research opportunities.

name: Subree Lab
title: Direct Inquiry Cancer Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: High school students interested in research are welcomed to inquire about joining the lab during the summer. Undergraduate students may also contact the lab and are encouraged to provide a résumé and statement describing their research interests.
ratingNote: A particularly strong opportunity for pre-med and biomedical students because the lab explicitly welcomes high school researchers during the summer and also provides a direct pathway for undergraduates to inquire about research positions.
summary: The Subree Lab at the University of Minnesota conducts biomedical research involving cancer biology, translational medicine, bioinformatics, and related approaches. The lab explicitly welcomes high school students interested in joining research during the summer. Undergraduate students are also encouraged to inquire and may submit a résumé and description of their research interests.

name: Dolmetsch Lab
title: Volunteer Biomedical Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: The lab accepts a small number of high school students each year. Interested high school students are instructed to email the lab with a one-page essay explaining why they want to work there. Undergraduate students from outside Stanford may also inquire about volunteer opportunities.
ratingNote: A rare direct-inquiry opportunity at Stanford for high school students interested in neuroscience and biomedical research. The lab explicitly states that it hosts a small number of high school researchers each year, although positions are likely highly competitive.
summary: The Dolmetsch Lab at Stanford University conducts biomedical and neuroscience research involving neurodevelopment, cellular signaling, and neurological disease. The laboratory accepts a small number of high school students each year. High school applicants are asked to contact the lab with a one-page essay describing why they want to participate, while outside undergraduates may also inquire about volunteer research.

name: Summer Youth Science Fellowship
title: Structured Summer Cancer Research Program
university: University of California, Irvine — Cancer Research Institute
applicationWindow: The 2026 application cycle is closed. The program operates during the summer, and students interested in future participation should check the official program page for the next application cycle.
ratingNote: A strong pre-med and cancer research opportunity because students spend several weeks working alongside UCI researchers and receive direct research mentorship. The specialized cancer focus makes it especially valuable for students considering medicine, oncology, or biomedical science.
summary: The Summer Youth Science Fellowship at the UC Irvine Cancer Research Institute is a six-week research experience for high school students interested in cancer science. Participants work alongside UCI researchers in laboratory or research-team settings and are paired with research mentors while gaining exposure to cancer biology, population science, and biomedical research.

name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Summer Student Program
title: Structured Summer Biomedical Research Program
applicationWindow: Applications are offered through an annual summer program cycle. Students should consult the official Memorial Sloan Kettering program page for the next application opening and deadline.
ratingNote: An outstanding opportunity for students interested in medicine, cancer biology, or computational biomedical research. Participants conduct an extended mentored project at one of the country's leading cancer centers, making it one of the strongest pre-med-oriented listings in the database.
summary: The Memorial Sloan Kettering Summer Student Program provides high school students with an eight-week biomedical or computational research experience. Students are paired with research mentors and work on an individual project connected to the broader research of an MSK laboratory, gaining direct exposure to cancer science and professional biomedical research.

name: Missouri S&T Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering High School Research
title: Direct Faculty Research Opportunity
university: Missouri University of Science and Technology
applicationWindow: Research positions are posted based on current faculty availability. High school students should review the available projects and contact the listed principal investigator directly for details about joining a research project.
ratingNote: An exceptional engineering opportunity because the department maintains a dedicated page of research positions available to high school students and provides direct faculty contacts for individual projects. Students may work alongside university faculty, graduate students, and research teams on active engineering research.
summary: Missouri S&T's Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering department lists research opportunities specifically available to high school students. Projects vary with faculty availability and can cover areas such as advanced manufacturing, mechanical engineering, and aerospace-related research. Students identify a project that interests them and contact the listed principal investigator directly about participating.

name: Robotics & Autonomous Systems Lab (RASL)
title: Direct Inquiry Robotics Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: No fixed application cycle is listed. The lab encourages and provides research experiences to undergraduate and high school students, with participation dependent on available projects and mentorship.
ratingNote: A rare direct-access robotics opportunity at a major research university. The lab explicitly states that it encourages research experiences for both high school and undergraduate students, with exposure to advanced robotics, autonomous systems, virtual reality, and human-robot interaction.
summary: Vanderbilt's Robotics & Autonomous Systems Lab conducts interdisciplinary research involving autonomous robots, human-robot interaction, rehabilitation robotics, virtual reality, intelligent systems, and human behavior. Although primarily a graduate research laboratory, RASL explicitly encourages and provides research experiences for undergraduate and high school students.

name: Utah NeuroRobotics Lab
title: High School NeuroRobotics Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: The lab typically hosts one to two high school students each summer through its NeuroRobotics Summer Enrichment partnership. Availability is limited and students should review the lab's high school opportunities page for current participation information.
ratingNote: An unusually hands-on engineering research experience for high school students. Previous students have contributed to projects involving robotic exoskeletons, virtual and augmented reality, clinical diagnostic technologies, and human-subject experiments, providing exposure to real interdisciplinary engineering research.
summary: The Utah NeuroRobotics Lab develops technologies at the intersection of robotics, neuroscience, rehabilitation, and human-machine interaction. The lab hosts a small number of high school researchers, particularly through its summer enrichment partnership. Past high school participants have worked on exoskeletons, VR and AR systems, clinical diagnostic tools, and human-subject research.

name: Research Immersion in Materials Science & Engineering (RIMSE)
title: Materials Science Research Immersion
department: Materials Research Science and Engineering Center
applicationWindow: Participation and application timing vary by RIMSE program cycle. Interested students should review the UC San Diego MRSEC RIMSE page for current opportunities, eligibility requirements, and application information.
ratingNote: A strong engineering research opportunity that introduces students to authentic materials science research environments. The program is notable for bringing together participants at multiple educational levels, including high school students, undergraduates, graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and other researchers.
summary: Research Immersion in Materials Science & Engineering is an NSF-supported initiative through UC San Diego's Materials Research Science and Engineering Center. Participants gain experience with materials science and engineering research while working in research environments that can include high school students, undergraduates, graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, visiting scholars, and professional researchers.

name: SLAAM Engineering Summer Academy
title: Structured Summer Engineering Research Program
applicationWindow: The 2026 session ran July 6–17 and is now closed. Students interested in a future session should check the Rutgers Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering program page for updated application dates and requirements.
ratingNote: A solid engineering research experience for high school students interested in mechanical and aerospace engineering. Students conduct research projects and participate in applied engineering activities, although the program charges tuition and is more structured than the direct-access laboratory opportunities in the database.
summary: The SLAAM Engineering Summer Academy at Rutgers introduces high-achieving high school students to science and engineering research through the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. Participants spend part of each day conducting a research project and also complete applied engineering group projects. The 2026 program ran for two weeks and charged an $875 program fee.

name: VIMS Summer Aide Program
title: Paid Marine Research Opportunity
university: William & Mary — Virginia Institute of Marine Science
applicationWindow: Summer positions depend on faculty research needs and available funding. A limited number of paid positions may be offered, while research-related volunteer opportunities may also be available during the summer or academic year.
ratingNote: An excellent marine research opportunity because students may be selected directly for paid work based on active faculty research needs. VIMS also offers the possibility of research-related volunteer involvement, making this more flexible than many structured summer programs.
summary: The VIMS Summer Aide Program gives high school students opportunities to work with researchers in marine science fields such as fisheries, oceanography, ecology, and coastal research. A limited number of paid positions may be available depending on faculty needs and funding, and VIMS also notes that research-related volunteer tasks may be available during the summer or throughout the year.

name: Shoals Marine Laboratory — Investigative Marine Biology Laboratory
title: Field and Laboratory Marine Research Course
university: Cornell University / University of New Hampshire
applicationWindow: Offered as a summer field-intensive course through Shoals Marine Laboratory. Students should review the current course schedule and registration information for the next available session.
ratingNote: A strong hands-on marine research experience that goes beyond a typical summer class. Students conduct actual research projects in a field-station environment and gain exposure to marine biology, ecology, ecophysiology, and experimental methods.
summary: Shoals Marine Laboratory offers an intensive marine biology research experience on Appledore Island in the Gulf of Maine. Students participate in field and laboratory research projects while studying marine ecology, ecomechanics, and ecophysiology under marine scientists. The experience emphasizes learning scientific methods by conducting real research.

name: Duke Marine Lab STEM Pathways Internship
title: Paid Marine Science Internship
applicationWindow: The program is open to eligible high school students in Carteret and Craven Counties, North Carolina. Students should review the Duke Marine Lab program page for current summer dates, application deadlines, and stipend information.
ratingNote: A valuable paid marine science opportunity that combines direct exposure to Duke Marine Lab research with community science and outreach. Geographic eligibility is limited, but students who qualify can gain meaningful experience alongside marine researchers.
summary: The Duke Marine Lab STEM Pathways Internship allows local high school students to experience marine and coastal research alongside Duke University Marine Laboratory scientists. Participants also engage in community science and outreach activities. Eligibility is limited to students in Carteret and Craven Counties, North Carolina, and summer stipends may be available.

name: Bonnie Sue Internship
title: Marine Research Internship
university: William & Mary — VIMS Eastern Shore Laboratory
department: Virginia Institute of Marine Science — Eastern Shore Laboratory
applicationWindow: Eligibility is limited to students connected to Accomack and Northampton Counties, Virginia. Students should review the Eastern Shore Laboratory internship page for the current application cycle, eligibility rules, and deadlines.
ratingNote: A highly specialized marine research internship where students assist VIMS scientists with active projects in aquaculture, fisheries, water quality, habitat, and coastal ecology. The geographic restriction makes it inaccessible to most students but especially valuable for eligible local applicants.
summary: The Bonnie Sue Internship at the VIMS Eastern Shore Laboratory gives high school and college students opportunities to assist scientists with ongoing marine research. Projects may involve oyster, clam, and scallop aquaculture, juvenile fish habitat, marine ecology, water quality, and environmental monitoring. Eligibility is tied to Accomack and Northampton Counties in Virginia.

name: See the Sea: CC Scholars
title: One-on-One Marine Research Mentorship
university: The University of Texas at Austin — Marine Science Institute
applicationWindow: The 2026 opportunity is specifically designed for eligible advanced seniors at Flour Bluff High School in Corpus Christi. Students should review the UT Marine Science Institute page for future cycles and updated eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: An exceptional one-on-one research experience for eligible students. Participants are paired directly with a graduate student, postdoctoral researcher, research associate, or scientist and complete an independent marine science project over an academic semester.
summary: See the Sea: CC Scholars provides advanced high school seniors with semester-long marine research mentorship at the UT Austin Marine Science Institute. Students are paired one-on-one with a graduate student, postdoc, research associate, or research scientist and conduct an independent real-world research project. The 2026 version is limited to eligible Flour Bluff High School seniors in Corpus Christi.

name: Markman Lab
title: Developmental Psychology Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: High school students interested in research with the lab are directed toward Stanford's RISE Summer Internship Program. Undergraduate research opportunities may also be available through the lab depending on current projects and mentor availability.
ratingNote: A strong developmental psychology opportunity because the lab provides a defined pathway for high school students to pursue research exposure through Stanford's RISE program.
